questions.question: Which findings support a hilar cholangiocarcinoma? Choose all that apply.
questions.explanation: An irregular hilar stricture with upstream dilatation and fibrous enhancement is typical.

questions.question: Which features suggest an aggressive bone lesion? Choose all that apply.
options: A thin stable sclerotic rim as the only finding
questions.explanation: A wide transition zone, cortical destruction and aggressive periosteal response indicate aggressive biology.

questions.question: Material that is high signal on T1 and suppresses on fat-saturated imaging is most likely:
questions.explanation: Fat is typically T1 hyperintense and suppresses with fat-suppression techniques.

questions.question: Which finding is particularly concerning in invasive fungal sinusitis?
options: Extrasinus spread with orbital or vascular involvement
questions.explanation: Extrasinus extension and vascular/orbital invasion are signs of aggressive invasive disease.

questions.question: Which findings are compatible with aortic coarctation? Choose all that apply.
options: Focal narrowing at the aortic isthmus
Inferior rib notching in longstanding cases
questions.explanation: Isthmic narrowing and systemic collateralisation are classic features.

questions.question: In a cirrhotic liver, a focal lesion with non-rim arterial hyperenhancement and washout should raise concern for:
options: A classic haemangioma in every case
questions.explanation: In an appropriate high-risk population, this enhancement pattern is characteristic of HCC.

questions.question: Portal venous gas in a patient with severe abdominal pain and CT signs of bowel ischaemia:
options: May indicate advanced ischaemic injury and requires urgent assessment
questions.explanation: Portal venous gas can be a serious finding when combined with clinical and imaging evidence of bowel ischaemia.

questions.question: Which approaches can reduce metal artefact on CT? Choose all that apply.
options: Higher photon energy in selected cases
Always reducing mAs to the lowest possible value regardless of noise
questions.explanation: Acquisition optimisation and dedicated reconstruction can reduce metal artefact.

questions.question: Which ultrasound findings support ileocolic intussusception in a child? Choose all that apply.
options: A completely normal bowel wall pattern
questions.explanation: Characteristic concentric rings and the longitudinal pseudokidney appearance support intussusception.

questions.question: A radiologist identifies a critical unexpected intracranial haemorrhage. Appropriate management includes:
options: Prompt direct communication to the responsible clinical team and documentation
Waiting for the routine report to be read the following week
Deleting the finding from the report
Communicating only if the patient calls
questions.explanation: Critical findings require timely communication through an appropriate closed-loop process.

questions.question: Which is a recognised complication of percutaneous transthoracic lung biopsy?
options: Portal vein thrombosis in every case
questions.explanation: Pneumothorax is one of the most common complications of transthoracic lung biopsy.

questions.question: Which HRCT findings support a usual interstitial pneumonia pattern? Choose all that apply.
options: Diffuse centrilobular nodules as the dominant pattern
questions.explanation: UIP is characterised by basal/subpleural fibrotic change, traction bronchiectasis and often honeycombing.

questions.question: On CT venography, a filling defect within a dural venous sinus with compatible symptoms suggests:
options: Normal arachnoid granulation in every circumstance
questions.explanation: Venous sinus thrombosis may appear as a filling defect and requires clinical/imaging correlation.

questions.question: Before an image-guided biopsy, which factors should be reviewed? Choose all that apply.
options: Whether tissue sampling will change management
questions.explanation: Appropriateness, access planning and haemostatic risk are core pre-procedural considerations.

questions.question: Which process best reduces the risk of wrong-patient or wrong-site radiological procedures?
options: Structured identity, procedure and site verification before intervention
questions.explanation: Standardised pre-procedural verification reduces preventable procedural errors.

cases.title: Obstructing ureteric stone
cases.stem: Non-contrast CT shows a distal ureteric calculus with ipsilateral hydroureteronephrosis.

questions.question: What is the principal imaging diagnosis?
options: Obstructive uropathy due to a ureteric calculus
questions.explanation: A ureteric calculus with proximal collecting-system dilatation indicates obstruction.

questions.question: Which additional CT finding would increase concern for an infected obstructed system?
options: Perinephric inflammatory change in a febrile patient
A phlebolith remote from the ureter
questions.explanation: Inflammatory change combined with clinical sepsis increases concern for infected obstruction.

cases.title: Displaced femoral neck fracture
cases.stem: An elderly patient has a displaced intracapsular fracture of the femoral neck.

questions.question: Which important complication is associated with this injury?
options: Avascular necrosis of the femoral head
questions.explanation: Disruption of retinacular blood supply places the femoral head at risk of avascular necrosis.

questions.question: Why does the intracapsular location matter?
options: The blood supply to the femoral head may be disrupted
questions.explanation: Intracapsular fractures may disrupt the vessels supplying the femoral head and also carry a risk of non-union.

cases.title: Vomiting and abdominal distension
cases.stem: An adult presents with colicky abdominal pain, vomiting and distension. Contrast-enhanced CT is performed.

images.imageQuery: small bowel obstruction CT transition point

questions.question: What is the principal diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Dilated proximal small bowel with a transition to decompressed bowel indicates mechanical obstruction.

questions.question: Which finding would raise concern for strangulation?
options: Reduced mural enhancement with mesenteric congestion
questions.explanation: Reduced enhancement and mesenteric/venous abnormalities can indicate compromised perfusion.

cases.title: Sudden focal deficit and headache
cases.stem: A patient presents with acute neurological symptoms. Non-contrast CT shows an extra-axial hyperdense collection.

questions.question: A crescentic extra-axial collection is most consistent with:
questions.explanation: Subdural blood spreads along the cerebral convexity and is typically crescentic.

questions.question: Which feature should be specifically reported?
questions.explanation: Mass effect and shift influence urgency and neurosurgical management.

cases.title: Acute mesenteric ischaemia
cases.stem: A 75-year-old patient with atrial fibrillation has sudden severe abdominal pain and an elevated lactate. CTA is performed.

questions.question: A proximal superior mesenteric artery filling defect most strongly supports:
questions.explanation: Acute arterial occlusion in this clinical context is highly suspicious for embolic mesenteric ischaemia.

questions.question: Which bowel finding most increases concern for infarction?
options: Absent mural enhancement with pneumatosis and portal venous gas in the appropriate context
questions.explanation: Loss of enhancement and intramural/portal gas are worrying signs of advanced bowel ischaemia.

questions.question: Which report would be potentially unsafe?
options: Calling the arterial occlusion an incidental chronic finding despite acute symptoms
questions.explanation: Failure to recognise acute mesenteric ischaemia can lead to bowel loss and death.

cases.title: Posterior fossa mass in a child
cases.stem: A 9-year-old child presents with headache and vomiting. Imaging shows hydrocephalus and a posterior fossa mass.

questions.question: A posterior fossa mass obstructing the fourth ventricle can cause:
questions.explanation: Obstruction of CSF pathways at the fourth ventricle can cause upstream hydrocephalus.

questions.question: Which features should be specifically assessed in the report?
options: Mass effect, hydrocephalus, herniation and tumour extent
questions.explanation: These findings determine urgency and surgical planning.

questions.question: Which omission would be potentially unsafe?
options: Failing to mention imaging signs of impending herniation
questions.explanation: Omission of impending herniation may delay emergency treatment.
